historical_record.description: The Spreckels Temple of Music, the bandshell on the Music Concourse, was built in 1900.

The Spreckels Temple of Music, the concourse's centrepiece, was built for the sugar magnate Claus Spreckels to designs by his architects the Reid Brothers, in Colusa sandstone with carving by Robert I. Aitken; 75,000 people came to its dedication on Admission Day, 1900, to hear Angelo Spadina's eighty-piece Park Band.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the second contract for rehabilitating the Spreckels bandstand in the Music Concourse to Arthur W. Baum at $5,469.
Claus Spreckels was building the music stand at his own expense, at a cost of about $75,000.
The Park Band moved here from the old music grounds.
